title: MZ Using a plugin for holding data?

posts.author: lilydark
posts.body:
I just started using RPG Maker (MZ), so I'm a total beginner. I'm kinda just hacking my way thru, just for context, so I definitely need the "explain it to me like I'm an idiot" version of stuff.
Anyway, I had this idea that instead of using a bunch of global variables for some things I need to set and have the game remember, I could define stuff in a plugin and then access it in my main plugin. I know there's parameters that can be accessed, but I need to be able to change them over time, and I dunno how to do that.
I looked at a bunch of other plugins that use registerCommand, and I thought there might be a way to make a command that would change params when I need to do that? I dunno. If anyone has a suggestion, that'd be cool. Thanks!

posts.author: lilydark
posts.body: Yeah, so, what I'm trying to do is make something that lets me set up dungeons really easily. So the storage plugin holds all that stuff, and only gets called when you first enter the dungeon. But then the main plugin gets called every time you move to a different floor, and I don't wanna have to set all that stuff every floor. I wanna have it set up once and then just use it or change it in that central place. Like I said, I know I could do it with global variables, but I also know that global variables are kinda scary, so I figured maybe this way would be better. Maybe it isn't better, tho.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
It's hard to recommend anything when your descriptions are all very vague and you say things like "storage plugin that holds all that stuff". What type of data, how and when it's being called, referenced, and modified, does the player modify it through inputs, is it being saved to the save file, etc?
Also when you say things like "global variables are kinda scary", it implies you don't know what you're doing when it comes to scripting, in which case you should not be writing your own plugins.

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
plugin commands works inside the register, not outside.
if you want to call it outside that, you need to call it different.
depending what the plugin does.
JavaScript:
//sample

function dataTopMap(...args) {
    let mymap = Number.args["topmap"]
    return $gameSystem._topMap
}
I cannot tell how the data is stored and where, but this is just a sample.
so you probably need to return the value to the sprite map is used there or
whatever you target it for.
if it's more for parallax, there are some out there for MZ, so you can look
how they did that as I'm not familiar with MZ, only MV, but the commands works
different there, so it's hard to tell.
as both support ES5 through ES8, MZ maybe higher, console log should
print correctly, if it does, target it correctly as well to be shown.
